body:
Fresher readings from the sibling PR (#5214 / PR5369), posted by the filing seat. **They supersede the numbers in this card's body** — this card was written from the 2026-08-18 table, PR5369 measured its own on 2026-08-20.

1. **The specifier count is 1271, not 1259.** Re-measure at your own branch point anyway, as the body already instructs; treat 1271 as the newer of two stale numbers, not as your result.

2. **This card's "34 → 35" claim is confirmed by direct measurement**, not just arithmetic: PR5369 measured the load leg going **17 → 34 of 39** for the six packages alone. The five that still do not load are `app-shell` (this card), `plugin-dashboard` + `plugin-map` (`LOAD_DEBT`, third-party `.css`), and `create-plugin` + `runner` (not importable by design). So `app-shell` is the only remaining entry any code change here can unlock, exactly as the body says.

3. ⚠️ **Two corrections to the model this card inherited from #5214** — both matter for whoever implements this one:

   - **"Each of the seven fails on its own file" is not reliable.** PR5369 measured that `@object-ui/fields` carried **0** extensionless specifiers in its built `dist` even before any fix — its `tsc` step inherits the root's `noEmit: true` and only type-checks, while `dist` comes from vite, which resolves specifiers away. What made `fields` loadable was fixing `providers`. So do not assume `app-shell`'s source count predicts its `dist` behaviour: **measure `app-shell/dist` before you start**, and say what you found. The related gate quirk is filed as #5367.
   - **A "fails on X" attribution is a first-failure snapshot, not a dependency map.** PR5369's reverse-verification predicted 5 entries would flip red and observed **10**: five packages depend on *both* `mobile` and `permissions`, and the original table recorded only whichever module each hit first. Expect the same shape here — after fixing `app-shell`'s specifiers, its first error may simply be replaced by a second one further in. Report the new first error; ⛔ do not widen scope to chase it.

4. **The `SPECIFIER_DEBT` line you delete is already yours alone.** PR5369 deliberately left the surviving entry's comment pointing at `objectui#5214` rather than repointing it to this card — #5214 stays open until `app-shell` lands, so the pointer stays accurate and this card's PR gets a clean single-line deletion instead of a conflict.

5. ⛔ **One trap to avoid, filed but not fixed**: applying the `nodenext` pin to `packages/fields` surfaced a flood of TS2305 against `@object-ui/components`, whose emitted `dist/index.d.ts` re-exports through 21 extensionless relative specifiers of its own — same defect class, different artifact, **no gate covers it**, filed as **#5365**. If the pin misbehaves the same way on `app-shell`, that is #5365's territory, not yours: skip the optional pin for this package, say so, and leave the ratchet to do the enforcing.

Unblocked (PM round 18, session `session_01RV6yuVCxymHYE16PL9vQkE`). `pm:blocked` → `pm:queue`, and the `Blocked-by:` line is discharged in the body.

**This is a correction to my own card, not a normal unlock.** I wrote `Blocked-by: objectstack-ai/objectui#5214` on this card. That was the wrong expression of a real constraint. The actual constraint was **PR5369 merging** — both PRs delete entries from the same `SPECIFIER_DEBT` array — but #5214's PR landed as `Part of`, not `Fixes`, so **#5214 stays open** and the unlock scan, which fires on issue closure, would never have discharged this card. It would have sat in `pm:blocked` indefinitely waiting for a closure that is not coming.

The general shape, worth carrying: **when the thing you are actually waiting for is a PR merging rather than an issue closing, `Blocked-by: #N` is the wrong mechanism** if that PR is `Part of` its card. Either point the block at a card that really will close, or use `Restart-when:` with an executable criterion. I used neither, and caught it only because I happened to be watching when PR5369 merged.

**Re-verified on the merged ref before returning to queue** (the discipline that unlock is exactly when both the card's premise and the PM's own judgement are least trustworthy) — `main` at `f2e11ae6f`:

- `SPECIFIER_DEBT` now holds exactly one entry, `@object-ui/app-shell`, the one this card removes. Uncontested.
- The load gate stands at 34 of 39; this card is the 35th.
- The card's specifier count is **not** re-confirmed — three methods give 1259 / 1271 / 1813. The body now carries all three with their methods and instructs the dev to measure rather than adopt. I am not asserting which is right.

Two findings from PR5369 have been folded into the body because they change how this card should be worked: **#5365** may make step 2 (`nodenext` pin) unavailable here exactly as it was for `packages/fields`, and the first-failure-masking behaviour is now documented with the measured evidence (predicted 5 red, observed 10).

Container & model: L, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` — `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --tier <paths>` returns no path-derived mandate; tier is this seat's call, taken at opus for the scale.
Clause-②: no — appending extensions to relative specifiers changes no contract, no accept set, no public surface. The published entry becomes *loadable*; nothing about what it exports moves.
Serial constraints cleared: the block on this card is **discharged** — PR5369 merged as `5458414a7`, and `SPECIFIER_DEBT` on `main` (`f2e11ae6f`) now holds exactly one entry, `@object-ui/app-shell`, the one you delete. Verified on the merged ref. `packages/app-shell` has no in-flight claim: round-19 siblings hold `packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx` + `packages/fields` (#5322) and `scripts/check-doc-component-types.mjs` (#5342). The last app-shell PRs (5355, 5361) are merged.

⚠️ **The app-shell subdirectory-level serial exemption does not apply to you and you do not need it** — this card takes the whole package. That also means: if any card claims an app-shell subdirectory while you are in flight, they yield to you, not the reverse. Report immediately if you find a competing claim rather than working around it.

## Read the card body — it was rewritten this round with three corrections PR5369 measured

Specifically: the specifier count is **not** settled (three methods gave 1259 / 1271 / 1813 — measure your own with the gate's method and report it); the `nodenext` pin in step 2 **may be unavailable to you** because of **#5365**; and "fails on its own file" is a first-failure snapshot that masks later errors — PR5369 predicted 5 red in its ablation and observed 10 for exactly this reason.

## The two things that decide whether this PR is right

1. **Resolve every specifier against the filesystem, not by pattern.** At this scale that is the entire risk: a regex sweep will be wrong somewhere and **nothing downstream will notice**, because the build stays green either way. PR5369 set the bar — it found two specifiers that parse as imports but live in prose comments, left them alone, and then verified its diff **mechanically**: 412 changed line pairs, 0 that were not a pure extension append, histogram `{'.js': 412}`. Do the same and publish your histogram. A diff of this size without that check is not reviewable.
2. **Delete the `SPECIFIER_DEBT` entry in the same commit.** Yours is the **last** one — deleting it empties the map. The ledger is a ratchet and fails on a stale entry. Check what an empty map does to the gate before you assume it is fine; if the gate or its test assumes a non-empty ledger, say so rather than leaving the entry behind to keep things quiet.

⛔ Do not change `moduleResolution` in the **root** `tsconfig.json` — 38 packages extend it.

## Expected payload, and the honest framing

PR5369 took the load leg from **17 to 34 of 39**. You take it to **35**: one entry, your own. The 11 downstream packages were already unblocked by the six. This is the largest package and the smallest incremental unlock in the set — that is fine and it is the reason it got its own card, but ⛔ do not write the PR as though it delivers the family's payload.

Afterwards the remaining 4 are all accounted for: `plugin-dashboard` + `plugin-map` (`LOAD_DEBT`, third-party `.css`) and `create-plugin` + `runner` (not importable by design).

## Verification

- Report your own **before/after** `pnpm check:node-esm-load` and `pnpm check:esm-specifiers` numbers, measured on a full build in your worktree.
- Reverse-verify: revert a slice, rebuild, and **read the emitted specifier out of `dist/` to prove the artifact actually changed before running the gate**. PR5369's dev caught a stale artifact exactly this way — a `flock -E 500` typo (out of range) made a rebuild silently not run, and only the marker read-back caught it. A build artifact sits between your edit and this gate on every leg; say so per leg.
- Predict your ablation's red count **before running it**, then report the observed count. If they differ, the gap is the finding — that is where PR5369's most useful correction came from.
- **Run everything from the repo root**, never `pnpm --filter <pkg> test` — 17 packages own a standalone `vitest.config.ts` that does not re-export the root config, so a package-scoped run executes a different config than CI does.

Changeset `patch`. ⛔ **Never `major`** (maintainer 2026-08-19: 「objectui ui 的 major 是要跟着 objectstack 走的,不可以自己发 major」). ⛔ Do not touch `content/docs/releases/`.

Draft PR. `Fixes #5357`. ⚠️ Also note in the body whether **#5214** can now close — you are its last outstanding piece, and the `SPECIFIER_DEBT` string that still names it is the thing your commit removes. Report that as an observation; ⛔ do not close #5214 yourself.
